passages.text: David again assembled the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand in all.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David gathered the chosen men of Israel.
He assembled thirty thousand men.
He did this again.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֥וֹד דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־ כָּל־ בָּח֥וּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃

passages.text: And he and all his troops set out for Baale of Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name— the name of the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim that are on it.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David gathered all the people who were with him.
They went from Baale of Judah.
They wanted to bring up the ark of God from there.
The ark of God is called by the Name of the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts sits enthroned between the cherubim on the ark.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם׀ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ מִֽבַּעֲלֵ֖י יְהוּדָ֑ה לְהַעֲל֣וֹת מִשָּׁ֗ם אֵ֚ת אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ נִקְרָ֣א שֵׁ֗ם שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יֹשֵׁ֥ב הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart, bringing with it the ark of God. And Ahio was walking in front of the ark.
passages.sermon:
David led the people of Israel.
They wanted to move the ark of God.
The ark of God was very holy.
The ark was at the house of Abinadab.
Abinadab lived on a hill.
They put the ark of God on a new cart.
Uzzah and Ahio were sons of Abinadab.
Uzzah and Ahio guided the new cart.
They brought the ark of God from Abinadab’s house.
Ahio walked in front of the ark.
passages.original: וַיַּרְכִּ֜בוּ אֶת־ אֲר֤וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ עֲגָלָ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֔הוּ מִבֵּ֥ית אֲבִינָדָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וְעֻזָּ֣א וְאַחְי֗וֹ בְּנֵי֙ אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב נֹהֲגִ֖ים אֶת־ הָעֲגָלָ֥ה חֲדָשָֽׁה׃ וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֗הוּ מִבֵּ֤ית אֲבִֽינָדָב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּבְעָ֔ה עִ֖ם אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְאַחְי֕וֹ הֹלֵ֖ךְ לִפְנֵ֥י הָאָרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
All the people of Israel were with him.
They celebrated before the LORD.
They used many kinds of instruments made of wood.
They played harps.
They played stringed instruments.
They played tambourines.
They played sistrums.
They played cymbals.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֣ד׀ וְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מְשַֽׂחֲקִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל עֲצֵ֣י בְרוֹשִׁ֑ים וּבְכִנֹּר֤וֹת וּבִנְבָלִים֙ וּבְתֻפִּ֔ים וּבִמְנַֽעַנְעִ֖ים וּֽבְצֶלְצֶלִֽים׃

passages.text: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen had stumbled.
passages.sermon:
Uzzah was the son of Abinadab.
Uzzah and his brother Ahio were guiding a new cart.
The cart carried the ark of God.
They brought the ark from the house of Abinadab.
The house was on a hill.
They came to the threshing floor of Nacon.
The oxen stumbled.
Uzzah reached out his hand.
Uzzah took hold of the ark of God.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־ גֹּ֣רֶן נָכ֑וֹן וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח עֻזָּ֜א אֶל־ אֲר֤וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ וַיֹּ֣אחֶז בּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י שָׁמְט֖וּ הַבָּקָֽר׃

passages.text: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
passages.sermon: The LORD became very angry with Uzzah.\r\nGod struck Uzzah down immediately.\r\nUzzah died there next to the ark of God.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּעֻזָּ֔ה וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ שָׁ֛ם הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עַל־ הַשַּׁ֑ל וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁ֔ם עִ֖ם אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah; so he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David saw what the LORD did to Uzzah.
The LORD struck Uzzah down.
David became angry because the LORD punished Uzzah.
David named that place Perez-uzzah.
People still call it Perez-uzzah today.
passages.original: וַיִּ֣חַר לְדָוִ֔ד עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּרַ֧ץ יְהוָ֛ה פֶּ֖רֶץ בְּעֻזָּ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֞א לַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ פֶּ֣רֶץ עֻזָּ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: That day David feared the LORD and asked, “How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
On that day, David saw what happened to Uzzah.
God struck Uzzah down beside the ark because Uzzah acted irreverently.
David became afraid of the LORD that day.
David said, “How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”
passages.original: וַיִּרָ֥א דָוִ֛ד אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵ֛יךְ יָב֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So he was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David did not want to bring the ark of the LORD to the City of David.
David decided not to move the ark to his city.
David took the ark of the LORD to the house of Obed-edom.
Obed-edom was a Gittite.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֣ה דָוִ֗ד לְהָסִ֥יר אֵלָ֛יו אֶת־ אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָ֖ה עַל־ עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּטֵּ֣הוּ דָוִ֔ד בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד־ אֱד֖וֹם הַגִּתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household.
passages.sermon:
The ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
It remained there for three months.
The LORD blessed Obed-edom.
The LORD also blessed all his household.
passages.original: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ אֲר֨וֹן יְהוָ֜ה בֵּ֣ית עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם הַגִּתִּ֖י שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־ כָּל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now it was reported to King David, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.” So David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing.
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
Someone reported news to King David.
The person said, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom.
The LORD has blessed everything that belongs to Obed-edom.
The LORD did this because of the ark of God.”
David heard this news.
David went to the house of Obed-edom.
David brought the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom.
David brought the ark into the City of David.
David did this with great joy.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בֵּרַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ בֵּ֨ית עֹבֵ֤ד אֱדֹם֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֔וֹ בַּעֲב֖וּר אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וַיַּעַל֩ אֶת־ אֲר֨וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים מִבֵּ֨ית עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם עִ֥יר דָּוִ֖ד בְּשִׂמְחָֽה׃

passages.text: When those carrying the ark of the LORD had advanced six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
passages.sermon:
Men carried the ark of the LORD.
They walked six steps.
David sacrificed an ox.
David also sacrificed a fattened calf.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּ֧י צָעֲד֛וּ נֹשְׂאֵ֥י אֲרוֹן־ יְהוָ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֣ה צְעָדִ֑ים וַיִּזְבַּ֥ח שׁ֖וֹר וּמְרִֽיא׃

passages.text: And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD, while he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sounding of the ram’s horn.
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
David wore a linen ephod.
David danced with all his strength before the LORD.
All the house of Israel joined David.
They brought up the ark of the LORD.
They shouted loudly.
They blew the ram’s horn.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֛ד מְכַרְכֵּ֥ר בְּכָל־ עֹ֖ז לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְדָוִ֕ד חָג֖וּר אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃ וְדָוִד֙ וְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מַעֲלִ֖ים אֶת־ אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה בִּתְרוּעָ֖ה וּבְק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃

passages.text: As the ark of the LORD was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
passages.sermon:
The ark of the LORD entered the City of David.
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
Michal looked down from a window.
Michal saw King David.
King David was leaping before the LORD.
King David was dancing before the LORD.
Michal despised David in her heart.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה בָּ֖א עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וּמִיכַ֨ל בַּת־ שָׁא֜וּל נִשְׁקְפָ֣ה׀ בְּעַ֣ד הַחַלּ֗וֹן וַתֵּ֨רֶא אֶת־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ מְפַזֵּ֤ז וּמְכַרְכֵּר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּ֥בֶז ל֖וֹ בְּלִבָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: So they brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David and the people brought the ark of the LORD to Jerusalem.
They placed the ark in its place.
They set the ark inside the tent.
David had pitched this tent for the ark.
David offered burnt offerings before the LORD.
David also offered peace offerings before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיָּבִ֜אוּ אֶת־ אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּצִּ֤גוּ אֹתוֹ֙ בִּמְקוֹמ֔וֹ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאֹ֔הֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָה־ ל֖וֹ דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּ֨עַל דָּוִ֥ד עֹל֛וֹת לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וּשְׁלָמִֽים׃

passages.text: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David finished offering burnt offerings.
David finished offering peace offerings.
David blessed the people.
David blessed them in the name of the LORD of Hosts.
passages.original: וַיְכַ֣ל דָּוִ֔ד מֵהַעֲל֥וֹת הָעוֹלָ֖ה וְהַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם בְּשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Then he distributed to every man and woman among the multitude of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake. And all the people departed, each for his own home.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
He gave gifts to all the people of Israel.
He gave gifts to every man and every woman.
He gave each person a loaf of bread.
He gave each person a date cake.
He gave each person a raisin cake.
All the people left.
Each person went to his own home.
passages.original: וַיְחַלֵּ֨ק לְכָל־ הָעָ֜ם לְכָל־ הֲמ֣וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ לְמֵאִ֣ישׁ וְעַד־ אִשָּׁה֒ לְאִ֗ישׁ חַלַּ֥ת לֶ֙חֶם֙ אַחַ֔ת וְאֶשְׁפָּ֣ר אֶחָ֔ד וַאֲשִׁישָׁ֖ה אֶחָ֑ת וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ לְבֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: As soon as David returned home to bless his own household, Saul’s daughter Michal came out to meet him. “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” she said. “He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, like a vulgar person would do.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David returned home.
He wanted to bless his own household.
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
Michal came out to meet David.
Michal spoke to David.
She said, “How the king of Israel has honored himself today!”
She said, “He uncovered himself today in front of the maidservants of his servants.”
She said, “He acted like a vulgar person would act.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֥שָׁב דָּוִ֖ד לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ בֵּית֑וֹ וַתֵּצֵ֞א מִיכַ֤ל בַּת־ שָׁאוּל֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מַה־ נִּכְבַּ֨ד הַיּ֜וֹם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִגְלָ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ לְעֵינֵ֨י אַמְה֣וֹת עֲבָדָ֔יו כְּהִגָּל֥וֹת נִגְל֖וֹת אַחַ֥ד הָרֵקִֽים׃

passages.text: But David said to Michal, “I was dancing before the LORD, who chose me over your father and all his house when He appointed me ruler over the LORD’s people Israel. I will celebrate before the LORD, and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this. Yet I will be honored by the maidservants of whom you have spoken.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Michal.
David said, “I danced before the LORD.
The LORD chose me.
The LORD chose me instead of your father Saul.
The LORD chose me instead of all his family.
The LORD appointed me ruler over His people Israel.
I will celebrate before the LORD.
I will humble myself even more than this.
I will make myself low in my own eyes.
The maidservants you mentioned will honor me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִד֮ אֶל־ מִיכַל֒ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּֽחַר־ בִּ֤י מֵֽאָבִיךְ֙ וּמִכָּל־ בֵּית֔וֹ לְצַוֺּ֨ת אֹתִ֥י נָגִ֛יד עַל־ עַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשִׂחַקְתִּ֖י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ וּנְקַלֹּ֤תִי עוֹד֙ מִזֹּ֔את וְהָיִ֥יתִי שָׁפָ֖ל בְּעֵינָ֑י וְעִם־ הָֽאֲמָהוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתְּ עִמָּ֖ם אִכָּבֵֽדָה׃

passages.text: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.
passages.sermon: Michal was the daughter of Saul.\r\nShe had no children.\r\nShe remained childless until the day she died.
passages.original: וּלְמִיכַל֙ בַּת־ שָׁא֔וּל לֹֽא־ הָ֥יָה לָ֖הּ יָ֑לֶד עַ֖ד י֥וֹם מוֹתָֽהּ׃פ
